scope: Generic executable acceptance index. Narrative rationale and task state are maintained separately.

requirements.statement: Use Pydantic, PyArrow, DataFusion, NetworkX and deltalake with distinct responsibilities and one logical model.
Retain SQLite as a credible transactional alternative; justify the selected stack by types, revisions and interoperability rather than size.
Persist a typed relational core, not only JSON node/edge bags.
Preserve element/model/type identities, independent names and readable aliases.
Give relationships their own identities and explicit type registry with direction, endpoints, cardinality and traversal rules.
Store canonical relationship directions and derive inverse views instead of maintaining duplicate inverses.
Add typed interface, deployment, data-schema, behavior, requirement and notation details only when fields or constraints justify them.
Represent multi-party handoffs/interactions as first-class objects with typed participants.
Link evidence and decisions to elements, relationships, fields or releases without building a second evidence platform.
Nest owned values; normalize independently identified and shared objects.
Keep the explicit interface Arrow schema and its foreign references as an implementation example.
Use the tested Arrow/Delta/DataFusion type intersection, explicit nullability and UTC microsecond instants; avoid baseline unions and extension types.
Use small namespaced extensions only as an escape hatch; promote frequently queried meaning into typed fields.
Use strict Pydantic domain validation and explicit Arrow mappings; validate cross-record architecture independently.
Use DataFusion for relational queries, comparisons and tabular validation; qualify recursive SQL where needed.
Construct disposable NetworkX projections from release-selected records; return typed/Arrow results.
Implement named traversal policies and retain paths, versions and evidence; do not equate reachability with certain failure.
Keep domain mutation separate from queries; use bound scalar SQL parameters or expressions.
Distinguish source history, storage history and architectural history.
Do not equate a Delta table version with an architecture release or claim native multi-table atomicity.
Publish an immutable manifest pinning every required table version, schema/profile version, source digest and artifact.
Start with full snapshots of changed tables, reuse unchanged versions and avoid replay-based micro-edit event sourcing.
Use one writer, a publication lock and an expected-parent check; stage and read back before exposing a release.
Permit orphan staged versions after failure, but never publish partial architecture state.
Retain referenced Delta history and create self-contained milestone Parquet/manifest/schema/source/output archives.
Record semantic change sets with rationale, authorship, decisions, field-level changes, validation and impact.
Hash canonical semantic content, preserving ordered sequences; distinguish layout changes; keep CDF supplementary.
Give design alternatives separate scenario/model identities and baseline references.
Separate design disposition, implementation, qualification, client acceptance and evidence/review status.
Model BPMN behavior, UML ordering, ERD keys/cardinality and notation bindings explicitly; do not infer them from generic edges.
Separate semantic and layout versions and the four meanings of validation success.
Use ruamel.yaml, Jinja2, lxml, pytest, Hypothesis and the selected static type checker for their bounded roles; use the standard library for ordinary utilities.
Exclude overlapping dataframe, database, orchestration and ORM layers initially; do not import the whole pilot ontology stack.
Isolate Delta/DataFusion registration, retain a pinned-snapshot PyArrow fallback and normalize arro3 boundaries.
Keep application code Python-only, with one package/locked environment and no change to the separate book-library environment.
Keep narrative/decisions in Notion, executable permitted inputs in GitHub, compiled Delta local and dated exports in Dropbox.
Pin source revisions and digests, or authorized snapshots when immutable source versions are unavailable.
Expose baseline/change/validate/diff/review/persist/publish/output operations through a small API and CLI.
Start without partitioning, Z-ordering, elaborate compaction or custom indexes; rebuild the query catalog from the manifest.
Qualify round trips, same-release queries, semantic changes, interrupted publication, stale parents and historical schema migration.
Preserve unknowns, manual processes and evidence gaps; do not invent facts to satisfy structural checks.
Do not claim tested interoperability; retain immutable Parquet plus manifests as the simpler alternative.
Use RecordBatchReader / Arrow C Stream as the preferred streaming interoperability contract where qualified; retain a materialized PyArrow fallback.
Define a schema/field metadata policy; Arrow metadata may self-describe physical storage but cannot become hidden semantic authority.
Make semantic hashes independent of Arrow chunk layout; dictionary encoding remains optional and qualification-gated.
Build one manifest-scoped DataFusion query context per ArchitectureRelease rather than querying mutable latest state.
Cross-release comparisons register explicit named sides/namespaces and never resolve table versions implicitly.
Define versioned parameterized query recipes with input roles, parameter schema, expected result schema and qualification cases.
Capture DataFusion logical/optimized/physical plan evidence during qualification without incorporating engine plans into semantic architecture identity.
Prefer DataFusion built-ins; UDF/UDAF/UDWF/UDTF require a demonstrated capability gap.
Abstract version-pinned Delta reads behind SnapshotProvider implementations so interoperability can change without changing domain/release semantics.
Qualify PyArrow Dataset and Delta scan/Arrow-stream providers before replacing the materialized provider.
Use deltalake Python commit metadata to bind table commits to publication attempts/change sets where supported and tested.
Qualify deltalake application transaction markers for per-table retry/idempotency; never treat them as cross-table publication atomicity.
Use Delta constraints only for row-local persisted invariants; cross-table, graph and evidence rules remain application validations.
Treat persisted schema changes as explicit versioned migrations; do not automatically merge schemas during normal architecture publication.
Use Delta CDF/history as storage-audit evidence and semantic-diff cross-checks, not as the architecture change log.
Retention/checkpoint/vacuum policy must protect every Delta version required by a retained ArchitectureRelease manifest or milestone archive.
Keep partitioning, compaction tuning and Z-order outside the baseline until measured file-layout pressure justifies them.
Maintain and continuously test an exact Python PyArrow/DataFusion/deltalake/arro3 compatibility matrix on supported platforms; do not add a custom Rust implementation for capability completeness.
The canonical model/release is the only semantic source; notation and rendered artifacts are generated.
Every projected semantic object uses a stable NotationBinding back to a canonical object.
ViewDefinition explicitly owns view type, purpose/audience, membership, perspective/filter and layout profile.
LayoutProfile/LayoutArtifact are versioned separately from semantic view content.
ProjectionArtifact records release/view, mapping/generator version and semantic/source digests.
RenderArtifact records renderer/layout/platform/font/options/output provenance.
Validation distinguishes canonical structure, semantic/cross-model, notation, schema/syntax, renderer and real-world correctness.
C4 baseline includes landscape/context/container; component/dynamic are selective; deployment is conditional; code diagrams are excluded.
Structurizr generation uses deterministic identifiers, relationship IDs where needed and explicit stable view keys.
Structurizr implied relationships are disabled in baseline generated workspaces.
Structurizr view membership derives from canonical ViewDefinition rather than uncontrolled wildcard/inference behavior.
Structurizr tags/properties/static perspectives derive from canonical metadata; external dynamic perspectives are excluded.
Generated Structurizr DSL does not use remote includes, scripts/plugins or duplicate narrative docs/ADRs as semantic inputs.
Structurizr automatic layout is baseline; any manual layout is a separate LayoutArtifact tied to a view digest.
Structurizr static export is the target rich C4 surface and portable PlantUML/SVG is a separate lower-fidelity artifact.
Filtered Structurizr views are not baseline for portable auto-layout output; use explicit views/perspectives.
Generate model-level ArchiMate Exchange XML as an interoperability artifact, never as the persistent source format.
Baseline ArchiMate Exchange covers model elements, relationships, modifiers, properties and optional organization metadata; diagram geometry is deferred.
ArchiMate concept/relationship validity is enforced by a versioned semantic mapping/relationship profile before export.
PlantUML ArchiMate is a visual projection separate from ArchiMate Exchange XML.
Use the selected PlantUML MIT distribution under a restrictive local security profile with no remote includes.
PlantUML aliases derive from canonical IDs; optional links/tooltips are presentation only and qualified for portal mode.
UML is selective: sequence/state where useful, class only when it materially clarifies implementation; BPMN remains workflow authority.
ERD is generated from actual schema keys/nullability/FKs/cardinality using a tested implementation-oriented notation.
PlantUML builds use syntax/failfast/timeouts and capture structured renderer diagnostics/provenance.
Renderer/layout-engine version is presentation provenance; byte-identical SVG across platforms is not a semantic acceptance requirement.
BPMN semantic XML and BPMN DI/layout are distinct versioned projection concerns.
The supported BPMN subset is explicit/versioned; unsupported constructs never silently downgrade.
BPMN qualification layers canonical validation, OMG XSD, bpmn-moddle, bpmnlint and renderer import separately.
bpmnlint correctness is the candidate technical lint set; recommended/opinionated rules remain advisory unless explicitly adopted.
bpmn-auto-layout is the preferred DI-generation candidate but must pass supported-subset, deterministic-layout, quality and packaging qualification before baseline adoption.
bpmn-js is the preferred local interactive renderer; the required bpmn.io watermark is preserved.
bpmn-to-image/Puppeteer is optional milestone export capability, not baseline runtime dependency.
If Node is introduced, it is a pinned vendor runtime/tool bundle, not a second application or persistent service by default.
Target Material for MkDocs 9.x as the offline-first portal theme only after exact-version lock/qualification.
Portal release output is offline/local first, with search/navigation/local assets and no analytics/comments/external runtime assets.
Generated portal routes for canonical elements/views/releases are stable and traceable to IDs.
Rich Structurizr C4 and qualified BPMN interactive views integrate with the portal without becoming editable sources.
Kroki is deferred/optional and, if enabled, is local, pinned and restricted; no public Kroki endpoint handles confidential models.
Vendor tools/runtime/schema versions, checksums, licenses/notices and security configuration are recorded.
ArchitectureRelease can pin projection/render/validation artifact digests and toolchain provenance.
Qualification proves cross-tool canonical identity consistency and runs relevant checks on macOS ARM64 and Linux x86-64.
Pydantic is the canonical runtime domain-validation layer; storage/rendering objects are not independently authored semantic models.
Authoring/domain records use strict validation and forbid undeclared extra fields by default.
Reusable semantic ID/version/digest concepts are represented by centralized constrained typed aliases rather than repeated raw-string rules.
Domain variants use explicit discriminated unions where a stable variant tag exists.
TypeAdapter is used only for natural type/collection boundaries and does not replace meaningful identified domain models.
Pydantic validators are limited to record-local rules and explicit deterministic validation context.
Cross-record/domain validation is implemented separately and returns structured Diagnostics without mutating records.
Published compiled Pydantic records are frozen and use immutable nested field types where semantic immutability matters.
Normal domain flows do not use model_construct, SkipValidation or equivalent validation bypasses.
Architecture mutation is expressed as validated typed ChangeCommands producing a fully revalidated candidate rather than arbitrary in-place model edits.
Pydantic validation failures are normalized into stable diagnostic codes, locations and structured context.
JSON Schema is a versioned generated authoring/machine contract with checked snapshots and discriminators.
Validation/serialization schema differences are introduced only deliberately and documented.
Canonical YAML authoring uses a controlled YAML 1.2 round-trip profile with explicit depth and output settings.
YAML duplicate keys are hard errors.
YAML anchors/aliases, merge keys, custom application tags and unsafe Python tags are forbidden in the baseline authoring profile.
ruamel presentation objects do not escape the authoring adapter into canonical domain/storage logic.
A SourceMap captures YAML semantic paths and line/column locations before conversion to Pydantic models.
Validation diagnostics resolve back to source file/line/column where authoring source exists.
Round-trip authoring edits reparse/revalidate and present a semantic diff before publication.
YAML comments, quote style, whitespace and semantically unordered key ordering are excluded from architecture semantic hashes.
NetworkX is a disposable release/candidate-derived analysis projection, not durable canonical storage.
NetworkX node keys are canonical object IDs and MultiDiGraph edge keys are canonical relationship IDs.
The raw NetworkX graph is encapsulated behind an ArchitectureGraph facade with no public general mutation API.
nx.freeze is treated only as a partial structural guard because graph attribute mappings remain mutable.
Graph queries use versioned GraphPolicy definitions with explicit edge types, directions, contexts, bounds and stopping rules.
Policy-specific read-only graph views use filtered/subgraph views where appropriate rather than duplicating graph state.
Graph impact/path results retain ordered relationship IDs and policy/release provenance.
Unbounded path enumeration is prohibited; depth/result/path caps are enforced before materialization.
Cycle, SCC, condensation and DAG analyses are used only under explicit graph semantics and retain mappings to canonical IDs.
Transitive reduction/closure results are derived analysis/view artifacts and never replace canonical relationships.
Jinja receives a fully prepared typed projection DTO; templates do not perform semantic graph/query/domain inference.
Jinja uses a centralized deterministic Environment with StrictUndefined and controlled loaders/whitespace/newline settings.
Jinja undeclared-variable analysis is used to qualify template/context contracts.
Custom Jinja filters/tests are pure deterministic presentation helpers.
Template bundle identity/digest includes transitive included/inherited templates that can change generated output.
Baseline Jinja templates are trusted checked-in toolkit code; arbitrary consumer templates are not supported without a separate sandboxed extension design.
Jinja is not used to generate BPMN/ArchiMate standards XML.
lxml standards XML generation uses structured namespace-aware APIs such as QName/ElementMaker.
All lxml parsing/validation uses an explicit no-network/no-DTD/no-external-entity/no-recovery secure parser baseline unless separately qualified.
Standards schema imports/includes resolve only through a reviewed checksummed local resolver.
lxml XMLSchema error logs normalize into structured validation diagnostics.
Relevant XML artifacts retain both literal source digests and canonical C14N digests; formatting-only XML changes do not masquerade as semantic changes.
Schematron/XSLT/incremental XML processing remain deferred until a concrete standards use case justifies them.
Hypothesis has reusable valid/invalid domain strategy libraries with bounded recursion and shrink-friendly construction.
Hypothesis rule-based stateful tests cover release publication failure/retry/stale-parent invariants.
Hypothesis profiles for dev/CI/deep qualification are explicit and version-controlled.
pytest uses registered qualification markers and a requirement marker spanning CORE/DATA/PROJ requirements.
A separate machine-readable pytest requirement-evidence report maps test outcomes to requirement IDs and implementation/platform provenance.
JUnit remains standard CI output; custom requirement evidence does not depend on nonstandard JUnit properties.
pytest fixtures are typed and use the narrowest practical scope; fault-injection tests are local/deterministic.
Known limitations use strict xfail with explicit upstream/version reason rather than silent broad exclusions.
Pyrefly is the target static type checker and replaces ty when the implementation cascade occurs.
Pyrefly is explicitly configured in pyproject for Python 3.14 and project source/tests/scripts rather than relying on basic/unconfigured mode.
The pinned Pyrefly version is lock-controlled and upgrades run full static/both-platform qualification because new versions may introduce new errors.
Pyrefly's built-in Pydantic support is qualified against every advanced Pydantic pattern the toolkit relies on.
Tests are type-checked and use Pyrefly's pytest fixture understanding.
Replaceable subsystem boundaries use typed Protocols where structural typing is appropriate.
Critical discriminated-union dispatch is statically exhaustive using narrowing/assert-never patterns where practical.
No Pyrefly baseline is used by default; suppressions are narrow error-code-specific reviewed exceptions.
Public toolkit API targets 100% strict Pyrefly type coverage after interface stabilization, with whole-src strict coverage tracked.
Pyrefly infer may assist local annotation work but never mutates source automatically in CI.
Ruff remains the formatter/linter with py314 target and existing E/F/I/UP/B baseline.
RUF/PT/PTH/S rule families are qualified against the codebase and enabled only with reviewed narrow exceptions.
Ruff preview behavior and unsafe automatic fixes are disabled in baseline CI.
Engineering/static check evidence is represented separately from architecture-model validation through EngineeringQualificationArtifact or equivalent implementation evidence.
The complete cross-library qualification matrix is executed before the GitHub implementation is described as satisfying the core architecture.
